messages.content: I need to put together a quick Denver work trip. I have a partner dinner Thursday evening and a sponsorship workshop Friday morning, then I can come home.
What are the dates, start times, and locations for the two commitments? Also, which Dallas airport can you use, and will you have a checked bag?

Thursday, May 8 and Friday, May 9. Dinner is at 6:30 p.m. near Union Station. The workshop starts at 9:00 Friday at 1675 Broadway and should finish at noon. I can use DFW or Love Field, and I will have one carry-on only.

That makes a same-day Thursday arrival workable, but I would avoid anything scheduled into Denver after about 3:30 p.m. A 4:00 p.m. arrival could leave too little protection against a delay, the airport train, hotel check-in, and the trip to dinner. For Friday, a departure after 2:30 p.m. gives you a reasonable path from the workshop to the airport. Should I compare the practical nonstop choices and one hotel night near the workshop?
Yes. Keep it in economy and show me the real total, including the airport transfer and getting between the hotel and dinner. I do not need a rental car.

I found three useful outbound patterns. Southwest from Love Field leaves at 9:05 a.m. and reaches Denver at 10:15 a.m. for $168. United from DFW leaves at 10:20 a.m. and arrives at 11:30 a.m. for $154. American from DFW leaves at 12:40 p.m. and arrives at 1:50 p.m. for $149. All are nonstop and the quoted fares allow a standard carry-on. The first two leave ample recovery time; American is still feasible, though a delay of roughly two hours would begin to threaten dinner.
Do not keep the American flight. What are the returns? I need enough time after noon to leave the workshop without rushing out early.

The strongest returns are Southwest to Love Field at 3:35 p.m., arriving 6:35 p.m., for $181; United to DFW at 4:10 p.m., arriving 7:15 p.m., for $163; and United at 2:25 p.m., arriving 5:30 p.m., for $142. I would remove the 2:25 option. From 1675 Broadway, leaving at noon gives only about 2 hours 25 minutes until departure, and downtown-to-airport disruption or security lines could erase the margin.
Agreed. Compare the two later returns with the two outbound choices. Also check hotels that are genuinely convenient for Broadway, not just labeled downtown.

Two one-night hotels fit well. The Holiday Inn Express Denver Downtown is about a five-minute walk from 1675 Broadway and totals $219.46 with taxes; breakfast and Wi-Fi are included. The Hilton Garden Inn Denver Union Station totals $207.18, but it is roughly a 25-minute walk or a short paid ride from the workshop. It is closer to Thursday's dinner and the airport train. Both offer cancellation until 6:00 p.m. local time on May 7 at the rates shown.
The Holiday Inn sounds easier Friday. How would the ground transportation work from the airport Thursday and to the airport Friday?

Take the A Line from Denver Airport to Union Station on Thursday; the airport day pass is $10 and covers that train plus eligible local transit for the day. From Union Station, a rideshare to the Holiday Inn is approximately $14 before tip. For dinner, allow about $12 each way by rideshare, or walk if the weather is good and you have time; it is around 20 to 25 minutes. Friday, a rideshare from the hotel to the airport is approximately $48. That is the more dependable choice after the workshop because returning to Union Station first adds a transfer and more timing variability.
Use rideshares for dinner both ways. Now total all four flight combinations with that hotel and those transfers.

Using $84 for ground transportation—$10 airport train pass, $14 Union Station to hotel, $24 round trip for dinner, and $36 as the current advance estimate for Friday's airport ride—the totals are: Southwest outbound plus Southwest return, $652.46; Southwest outbound plus United return, $634.46; United outbound plus Southwest return, $638.46; United outbound plus United return, $620.46. These include airfare, the $219.46 hotel total, and estimated local transportation. They exclude meals and optional airline purchases. Because rideshare pricing can change, I would carry a $15 contingency, making the working ceilings $667.46, $649.46, $653.46, and $635.46 respectively.
You first said the airport ride was about $48, but the total uses $36. Which number is correct?

The $48 estimate is the appropriate conservative figure for an on-demand Friday ride. The $36 figure was an advance-booking quote and should not have been used as though it were dependable. Adding the missing $12 makes the corrected base totals $664.46, $646.46, $650.46, and $632.46. With a further $15 ground-transport contingency, the corresponding working ceilings are $679.46, $661.46, $665.46, and $647.46.
Thank you. Between the cheapest combination and the one using Love Field both ways, which has the better schedule margins?

The cheapest combination is United both ways: DFW 10:20 a.m. to Denver 11:30 a.m. Thursday, then Denver 4:10 p.m. to DFW 7:15 p.m. Friday. It gives about seven hours from scheduled arrival to dinner and four hours ten minutes from workshop end to departure. Southwest both ways leaves Love Field at 9:05 a.m., arrives 10:15 a.m., and returns at 3:35 p.m. Friday. It provides an extra 75 minutes before dinner but 35 minutes less after the workshop. Both margins are dependable; United is stronger on the tighter Friday leg and costs $32 less.
Then keep United both ways. Is there any concern about reaching dinner if the A Line has a problem?

You still have substantial protection. With an 11:30 a.m. scheduled arrival, even allowing 30 minutes to exit the terminal and 45 minutes for the train, you should reach Union Station around 12:45 p.m. If the train is disrupted, an airport-to-hotel rideshare generally takes 35 to 55 minutes in ordinary traffic. A two-hour flight delay would still put you downtown around 2:30 to 3:00 p.m. The plan becomes uncomfortable only if arrival slips beyond roughly 4:00 p.m.; at that point, skip the train, take a rideshare directly to the hotel, leave the bag, and go to dinner.
What time should I leave the workshop Friday, and does the hotel need to hold my bag?

Check out before the 9:00 a.m. workshop and ask the hotel to hold your carry-on. When the workshop ends at noon, retrieve it and request the rideshare by 12:20 p.m. A typical airport arrival would be about 1:05 to 1:20 p.m., leaving nearly three hours before the 4:10 departure. Even with a 45-minute traffic delay, you would retain more than two hours. Confirm that luggage storage is complimentary; if it is not, add the disclosed charge to the trip total.
Give me the final plan and the amount I should submit for approval. Include anything that still needs verification, but do not keep weaker alternatives.

Use United nonstop from DFW to Denver on Thursday, May 8, departing 10:20 a.m. and arriving 11:30 a.m., then United nonstop from Denver to DFW on Friday, May 9, departing 4:10 p.m. and arriving 7:15 p.m. The two economy fares total $317 with a standard carry-on. Stay one night at the Holiday Inn Express Denver Downtown, about a five-minute walk from the workshop, at a quoted tax-inclusive total of $219.46. Thursday, take the $10 A Line to Union Station, rideshare to the hotel for about $14, and budget $24 for rideshares to and from the 6:30 dinner. If the inbound flight lands after roughly 4:00 p.m., take a rideshare directly from the airport instead. Friday, check out before the workshop, leave the carry-on with the hotel, retrieve it at noon, and request a roughly $48 airport ride by 12:20 p.m. The estimated trip total is $632.46. Submit $647.46 for approval to include a $15 transportation contingency. Before booking, verify the exact flight numbers and fare rules, carry-on inclusion, the hotel's $219.46 mandatory total and May 7 cancellation deadline, complimentary luggage storage after checkout, and whether the hotel requires a deposit or incidental hold. Nothing has been booked.
